As discussed in a previous section, highly specialized personnel are needed for operation as well as routine and specialized maintenance. In addition to these facility and personnel considerations supply chain resiliency is a particular problem with advanced equipment. For this reason, spare components and multiple machines of the same type may be co-located to reduce risk of downtime; furthermore, machines from multiple OEMs may also be co-located to ensure reduce the risk of all equipment being inoperable due to an OEM supply chain issue. Housing multiple machines of the same make and operating characteristics accelerates weld development by enabling prototyping on reduced size mock-ups on a smaller chamber before moving to full size components larger machines. As discussed in the Maintenance and OEM Section OEMs with manufacturing and service facilities in the USA will have a faster support and repair time than other manufacturers. This is becoming increasingly important as supply chains are continually strained. While there are a number of EBW facilities throughout the United States, there is a large concentration of capabilities in the Chicago area, as it is a machine tool manufacturing hub as well as the headquarters of Sciaky. The Northeast sector host a number of EBW facilities as this is a major turbine engine manufacturing hub which supports suppliers such as GE Aerospace and Pratt & Whitney. California host a number of high quality EBW shops in support of aerospace, defense and semiconductor industry.
